title: 1991 AHSME Problem 14
statement: If \(x\) is the cube of a positive integer and \(d\) is the number of positive integers that are divisors of \(x,\) then \(d\) could be

solutions.text:
For any prime \(p,\) take \(x=p^{201}=(p^{67})^3.\) This is a cube, and its positive divisors are \(1,p,p^2,\ldots,p^{201},\) a total of \(202.\) Thus \(202\) can occur.

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: In the prime factorization of a cube, every exponent is divisible by \(3\)
Try a cube having only one prime factor
